verdict.rationale: Phaser's ecosystem includes a first-party hosted Game Agent that takes plain-language game requests ("What game do you want me to make?"). The Phaser Editor page also describes an assistant that performs scene tasks such as creating particle emitters and reorganising layers "without switching tools." Evidence for a built-in assistant is thin marketing copy, though: much of the agent material describes external coding agents (Claude, Cursor, Copilot) driving the MCP server rather than an assistant built into the product, and the core Phaser framework itself has no assistant. missing for 10: detailed first-party docs on the in-product assistant's capabilities and limits, clear evidence the assistant is native to the editor rather than external agents via MCP, independent or hands-on corroboration of task delegation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: What game do you want me to make? Click Surprise Me for a random idea!
Create a particle emitter, reorganise a scene into layers, rename a bunch of objects — it handles it without switching tools.
